test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Suppose a magic mirror is placed in front of a boy. As a result, the boy observes that the image of his head is of the same size, the middle portion of his body is smaller and that of his legs is bigger. Hence, from top to bottom, the magic mirror displays which of the following images?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plane, convex and concave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **A plane mirror** produces images that are of the same size as the object; hence, the boy’s head appears to be of the same size.
 
• A convex mirror diverges light rays and forms smaller images, making the middle portion of the boy’s body appear smaller.
 
• A concave mirror converges light rays and can form magnified images, making the boy’s legs appear larger.
 
• The arrangement of plane, convex, and concave mirrors would create the observed effect from top to bottom.
 
• This specific combination of mirror types is used to create various optical illusions and is common in funhouse mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plane Mirror:**

 
 
• A plane mirror reflects light without changing the image size.
 
• The image is virtual, upright, and laterally inverted.
 
• Commonly used in everyday life, such as in bathrooms and dressing rooms.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors curve outward, causing light rays to diverge.
 
• Produces virtual, diminished, and upright images.
 
• Used in vehicle side mirrors and security mirrors for wider fields of view.
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• Concave mirrors curve inward, causing light rays to converge.
 
• Can produce real, inverted images or virtual, magnified images based on object distance.
 
• Used in applications like shaving mirrors, telescopes, and headlights.
 
 
 
• **Optical Illusions:**
 
 
• Optical illusions are visual phenomena where the perceived image differs from reality.
 
• Utilize various types of mirrors to create exaggerated or distorted images.
 
• Commonly found in amusement parks, funhouses, and art installations.
